findings.title: Validate the intercepted final positive against its consumer contract before credit or restatement
findings.evidence: candidate_reply_problem validates the text grammar and permits either 12 or 16 words, but does not reject nonfinite words. It accepts TEST at scene zero with an empty name and accepts any nonempty name for a nonzero scene. The new intervention then counts a 12-word TEST as eligible, changes held subtype and returns the later real mirror refusal. Core therefore never receives the original positive and cannot run its raw-finite, nonzero TEST scene and exact scene-name checks.
findings.effect: A malformed positive can be hidden by the expected counterfactual refusal, falsely proving that a valid final pose consumed the held rule. The positive-first harness does not damage these acceptance fields at the interception point.
minimum_correction: Before eligible credit, held-state mutation or extra evaluation, require the intercepted final nonmobile TEST to satisfy the relevant actual consumer contract: nonzero scene, exactly twelve grammar-valid raw finite binary32 words and the exact expected scene-name echo. Use integer/text word classification, without loading the words as floating values.

Use an existing authoritative scene-name source, not a guessed name or an independently loaded model image. The already naturally delegated object/custom_object metadata replies echo compiled_scene_name(scene) (model_host.rs 1761-1781); their completed-boot acceptance can establish a scene-to-name binding. The current wrapper retains no such map. Missing or inconsistent binding must not permit credit or mutation.

Add positive-first single-fault controls for nonfinite positive words (including signaling NaN), TEST scene zero and wrong nonempty scene echo. Each must fail as its positive reply fault with zero rule restatement and zero extra evaluation; no damaged native experiment is required. Keep the coherent positive, subtype-only strict ACK and named real refusal controls.
findings.grouping: One bounded positive-consumer-contract group; no production API, new store, solver or expanded native programme is requested.

review_conclusions.design_supported: A city-listed fixed-family building is a legitimate consumer of the held subtype-derived collision rule once the actual placement facts are given. The unmodified real provider is delegated to first; the additional same-payload evaluation is explicitly Host-only, not a second campaign question.
review_conclusions.identity_and_state: The intervention requires the current served placement/child join, a held acknowledged fixed report, a nonzero original subtype, final placement facts and the real positive answer. It copies the cached 16-word fixed report and changes only subtype to valid UNKNOWN. It uses the same provider and identical scene/depth/kind/definition/key arguments.
review_conclusions.ack_and_failure_accounting: The full fixed-report reply validator requires placed, same key and no cursor. Failed ACKs set a separate failure and prevent reevaluation. Answered or raised reevaluation records a failure, not credit. A successful case requires exactly one changed state and the exact mirror/collision-fixed refusal, with request faults zero and reply faults one. Clean absence remains UNREACHED; unrelated fatal or earlier reply faults fail.
review_conclusions.side_effect_boundary: With coherent original input and acknowledged UNKNOWN restatement, fixed_join refuses the flag mismatch before candidate_in_store. The extra evaluation does not repeat a Core terrain, UPDATED, movement, RNG or time service. This source-supported boundary is narrower than claiming arbitrary duplicate provider calls are effect-free.
review_conclusions.clean_code: The new branch uses existing staged joins, cached reports and ACK validation without changing production ownership. Its interception makes complete positive validation a prerequisite; the shared partial reply checker is insufficient for this new purpose.
